subject: Immediate: Dedicated GPU pool saturation — request for cross-functional playbook and executive sign-off
messages:
From: Sara Diaz <sara@fastledger.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Support <support@fastledger.com>, procurement@fastledger.com
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Immediate: inference slowdowns and 5xx spikes in prod (FastLedger)

Hi Marissa / Jonas,

We're seeing a sustained increase in 5xx rates and tail latency from our reserved pool for the last 45m. Peak QPS is ~3.2x our committed throughput and token queuing is hitting ~1.2M pending tokens in KV cache across sessions. This is hitting checkout flows in production (users see payment retries).

Can Redwood do an emergency burst? We need a confirmed action within 60 minutes and an estimate for restored p99 latency. Procurement is copied for any paperwork.

Attaching the CSV with sample QPS/latency windows.

— Sara
Product Lead, FastLedger
(Attachment: fastledger_qps_metrics_10-22.csv)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Diaz <sara@fastledger.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Tim Chang <tim.chang@cloud-partner.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Immediate: Dedicated GPU pool saturation — request for cross-functional playbook and executive sign-off

Sara — thanks for the data. We're treating this as Priority P0 for FastLedger. Short summary of what we're seeing on Redwood:

- Reserved pool for FastLedger is at sustained slot utilization ~98% across the last 30 minutes.
- Autoscale headroom exhausted due to noisy-neighbor spike from an adjacent tenant that started batch jobs unexpectedly.
- KV cache growth amplified token queueing for long-chat sessions.

Immediate asks / actions I recommend now:
1) Emergency burst authorization: increase FastLedger reservation by +40% for the next 3 hours (billing/credits discussion to follow). If procurement approves, we can switch the reservation into a higher-capacity burst lane immediately.
2) Apply rapid routing fallback: divert 25% of traffic to a compatible quantized variant (gpt-xl-q8) running in a hot-standby pool in us-west. This reduces p99 by estimated 150–400ms but preserves correctness.
3) Start noisy-neighbor mitigation with infra: throttle the adjacent tenant batch window and reclaim slots.
4) Post-incident: we should codify a playbook and define burst SLAs (frequency, max duration, billing cadence).

I need one of the FastLedger execs to confirm emergency burst now (procurement is copied). Tim from our cloud partner is on standby for capacity reallocation if we need cross-zone migration.

Markus / Irene / Jonas — I'm escalating to you for exec sign-off path and quick approval of the billing/credit terms so ops can flip the reservation. I've attached a proposed burst terms PDF and our ops runbook excerpt for the playbook.

Marissa
Senior AC, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: proposed_burst_terms_v2.pdf)
(Attachment: runbook_gpu-throttle.md)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Immediate: Dedicated GPU pool saturation — request for cross-functional playbook and executive sign-off

Copying notes from infra ops and legal (summarized):

- Ops can perform a temporary reservation uplift to accommodate +40% burst for up to 4 hours without hardware reprovisioning, provided financial terms are acknowledged within the hour.
- Legal/procurement requires written authorization from FastLedger procurement (procurement@fastledger.com) and an approval from a Redwood exec for any manual crediting beyond standard overage terms.
- Fallback routing to gpt-xl-q8 is validated; quality regressions were measured at <2% on our eval set for FastLedger prompts.

Irene — can infra push the throttle for the noisy tenant and confirm slot reclaim ETA? Markus — can you confirm the exec approval channel and short wording we can send to procurement to lock the billable uplift? I will stand up an incident bridge and loop in CS/Eng.

Jonas
Head of Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference

On Thu, 22 Oct 2026 at 09:28, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Ops update: noisy tenant throttled; reclaimed ~18% of slots in 12 minutes. Remaining headroom shortfall ~22%. We can reclaim another 10% by pausing best-effort batch jobs across low-priority pools in 18m.
>
> ETA to full slot availability (without burst uplift) ~40 minutes.
>
> — Irene
> Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: procurement@fastledger.com <procurement@fastledger.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Diaz <sara@fastledger.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Immediate: Dedicated GPU pool saturation — request for cross-functional playbook and executive sign-off

Marissa / Jonas — procurement confirms we approve an emergency uplift for the next 3 hours. We will accept the proposed burst terms in proposed_burst_terms_v2.pdf and will circulate a PO for the uplift later today. Please execute the uplift now.

Additionally, FastLedger requests a formal post-mortem and a written playbook with clearly defined burst-fallback triggers, billing thresholds, and a contact roster for 24/7 approvals. We'll need that before agreeing to long-term burst frequency > 6/month.

Procurement Team
FastLedger
(Attachment: PO_pending_approval.pdf)
